experiment.claim: Issue #495 -- NOT a spec claim (spec/target-spec.md has no ratified POR_RAW-glitch, ramp or reset row as of this record). Replaces the mismatch-seed reproduction of the ss/-40C mc14 pulse (PR #491 replay-474) with a deterministic forced offset: a DC source VOFF in series with the gate of XMOL2 (the output leg of the OK detector's XMOL1/XMOL2 mirror) in a DERIVED copy of design/netlist/bias_core.spice, swept over -12..+12 mV, so the early-assertion / pulse behaviour has a repeatable testbench that does not depend on a mismatch seed. Every point is nominal-process (no _mm section): the offset is the only variation. Records, per point: the VDD at which BIAS_OK first asserts, every POR_RAW high interval on the UP segment other than the genuine release (pulse start/end VDD, width in volts and measured seconds), the genuine VPOR-up, and whether RESETn (real por_output_chain on the shared IBIAS) is released by a pulse. Each point is run under the default start, `uic`, and `gmin=1e-11` so solver-state dependence is stated, not assumed. Design and spec are unchanged.
experiment.statistical_convention: N/A (deterministic forced-offset sweep of the nominal drawn circuit, not a distribution claim). The offset axis is a sensitivity sweep; sigma_XMOL ~2.9 mV (issue #455) is used only to label +-3 sigma ~ +-9 mV input-referred.
experiment.title: Deterministic forced-offset reproduction of the early BIAS_OK assertion / POR_RAW release-then-reassert pulse (bias_core OK detector, real por_comparator + por_output_chain)

matrix.subset_reason: full-grid record: the three paired corners ss/-40C, tt/27C, ff/125C rather than the 15-point process x temperature matrix; the supply is the swept variable (0 -> 3.63 V), so there is no separate supply axis

tools.fleet_note: submitted as a `klt sim` deck-list (`decks[]`) request, the transport klt documents for a harness that renders its own decks and mints its own evidence from the raw logs (klayout-tools #2804): each point's deck is shipped byte-for-byte and run as `ngspice -b <deck>` in its own directory on the fleet worker, so the artifact is the one this harness mints rather than one klt re-composed from a corner axis. The per-point `.spiceinit` rides as a `decks[].inputs[]` entry, which is how a setting the fleet drops from `options.ngspice_init` still reaches the run
